forces.title: Leveraged PE-backed retailers face elevated restructuring risk
forces.description: Highly leveraged and private-equity-backed businesses in the UK retail sector are more exposed to restructuring risk. This highlights how financial structures, combined with pressures like Middle East developments, cost-of-living concerns, and margin erosion, intensify vulnerability for PE-backed firms, particularly mid-market players. The ability to adapt quickly to changing consumer behavior may be a key differentiator in determining survival for these businesses.

forces.title: Shift to operating performance for value creation in PE
forces.description: The PE industry is experiencing a structural shift where value creation is increasingly driven by operating performance rather than leverage or multiple expansion. Between 2010-2022, nearly 60% of buyout value came from leverage and multiple expansion. By 2025, with valuation multiples hitting a record 11.8x EBITDA, operating performance must carry more of the load, making price discipline and post-acquisition improvements critical for returns, requiring deeper operational engagement from PE firms.
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

forces.title: Digital infrastructure expansion driven by AI, diversifying portfolios
forces.description: The digital infrastructure universe is rapidly expanding to include AI infrastructure, such as data halls and power assets, alongside traditional communications assets. This diversification is increasing the opportunity set for investors, but also complicates portfolio management by increasing sensitivity to utilization and customer mix. Capital is abundant for core data centers and hyperscale platforms, while execution-heavy assets face wider valuation gaps and longer exit timelines, creating a more complex investment landscape for PE.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Increased holding periods and valuation gaps for complex assets
forces.description: The average infrastructure asset holding period increased to 7.6 years in 2025 (from 6.1 years in 2021), reflecting challenges for execution-heavy and transitional assets like B2C fiber and cable. These assets face wider valuation gaps and narrower buyer universes as investors reassess churn, capital intensity, and operating complexity. This trend complicates exits and portfolio management for PE firms in the digital infrastructure space, demanding more active asset management strategies.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Increased PE hold periods necessitate sustained value creation
forces.description: Private equity hold periods have lengthened to over 6.5 years on average, with only 19% of 2021 acquisitions sold by 2025, well below the historical 30% four-year exit rate. This structural shift, coupled with declining buyout distributions (6% of AUM in 2025 vs. 16% historical average), requires PE firms to adopt more adaptive, execution-led models for value creation throughout the ownership period, rather than relying on quick exits, fundamentally altering their operational approach.
forces.source_title: Unlocking full potential: Five practices reshaping PE value creation

forces.title: AI integration accelerates PE value creation and re-underwriting
forces.description: Building AI into portfolio companies can significantly accelerate value creation, with impacts such as 40% cost reduction in content production and 15% in customer care, while enabling new products. At the fund level, AI reduces re-underwriting time from weeks to days, allowing deal teams to test assumptions more frequently and deeply. This enhances portfolio monitoring and cross-portfolio analysis, making AI a powerful engine for improving asset performance and investment decisions, and ultimately boosting returns.
forces.source_title: Unlocking full potential: Five practices reshaping PE value creation

forces.title: PE firms expanding operating groups for deeper portfolio engagement
forces.description: Since 2021, PE firms have more than doubled the size of their operating groups, expanding specialized capabilities and engaging operating teams earlier in the investment life cycle. This reflects a shift towards enterprise transformation as the new normal, with over 80% of portfolio companies undergoing such changes. Investing in dedicated transformation leadership, such as Chief Transformation Officers, is gaining traction to support more intensive, sustained execution and accelerate value capture across portfolio companies.
forces.source_title: Unlocking full potential: Five practices reshaping PE value creation

forces.title: Climate adaptation financing: significant opportunity for private capital
forces.description: The UK requires an estimated £11bn annually for climate adaptation and resilience investments. Despite constraints like short-term private market horizons (3-5 years), there's a growing opportunity for private capital, especially through public-private partnerships and blended finance. These structures de-risk investments, improving risk-adjusted returns and attracting private capital to projects that reduce climate vulnerability and support insurability, aligning financial goals with environmental resilience.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Short-term PE horizons constrain climate resilience investment
forces.description: A key headwind for private equity in climate adaptation is the mismatch between long-term climate risk and typical 3-5-year private market investment horizons. Resilience investments, which deliver value over extended periods by reducing future losses, are often discounted in current decision-making. This structural disincentive leads to underinvestment in adaptation, even as risk awareness grows, making it harder for PE firms to justify upfront capital for long-dated, avoided-loss benefits, thereby limiting capital deployment in this critical area.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: AI-driven product transformation and new business creation
forces.description: Private equity firms have a significant opportunity to drive value by moving portfolio companies beyond basic AI productivity gains to product transformation and new business building. Companies embedding AI in products (Level 3) achieve 20x median revenue multiples, while those creating new AI-driven businesses (Level 4) reach 31x. This strategic integration of AI, especially in software companies (33x multiple), creates fundamentally more scalable revenue streams and significantly boosts revenue per employee, representing a major upside.
forces.source_title: Beyond productivity: How AI creates value in private equity

forces.title: Talent scarcity hinders PE portfolio AI value creation
forces.description: Talent scarcity is a significant barrier preventing PE firms from leveraging AI to its full potential across their portfolio companies. Despite the availability of low-code/no-code platforms, many companies are reluctant to build dedicated AI teams, particularly at lower maturity levels. This constraint slows the progression up the AI value creation ladder, risking missed opportunities for enhanced revenue multiples and efficiency gains that AI can provide beyond basic productivity, thus impacting portfolio performance.
forces.source_title: Beyond productivity: How AI creates value in private equity

forces.title: Low tech exposure dampens UK PE market attractiveness
forces.description: The UK private equity market is reportedly 'losing its magic', with its low exposure to the technology sector identified as a significant headwind. This lack of tech-focused investment limits the UK's PE market from capitalizing on high-growth, innovation-driven opportunities that are increasingly defining global private capital. This impacts competitiveness and overall returns, contributing to a perceived decline in market allure, potentially exacerbated by wider Brexit-related economic shifts and hindering future growth.
forces.source_title: Brexit 10 years on: What it means for UK businesses today

viewpoints.title: Purchase price discipline now critical for PE buyout fund returns
viewpoints.description: McKinsey analysis of PE buyout fund vintages (2018-2023) demonstrates that disciplined buying at lower purchase price multiples (PPMs) is now paramount for strong returns. The lowest-price quartile delivered 3.4x MOIC, while highest-PPM buyers achieved 2.7x. Top performers in the lowest quartile reached 5.5x MOIC, significantly outperforming best performers in the highest quartile (3.6x). This marks a shift from the 2010-2017 boom where market tailwinds cushioned elevated entry prices, making price discipline a core differentiator for success.
viewpoints.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

viewpoints.title: AI integration beyond productivity boosts PE-backed company valuations
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's analysis of 471 PE-backed companies (2023-2025) reveals that embedding AI across operations, products, and new business ventures significantly increases valuations. Companies broadly embracing AI trade at median revenue multiples more than double those focused solely on productivity. Firms achieving 'business building' with AI (Level 4) showed a 31x revenue multiple, a 52% jump in revenue per employee over Level 3, significantly outperforming those with opportunistic or operational AI adoption, highlighting AI as a major value driver.
viewpoints.source_title: Beyond productivity: How AI creates value in private equity

viewpoints.title: UK private equity market losing allure, hindered by low tech exposure
viewpoints.description: Allianz Trade's 'Brexit 10 years on' report indicates that the UK private equity market has 'lost its magic'. A key contributing factor is highlighted as the market's 'low tech exposure'. This suggests that the UK PE sector may be lagging in capturing growth opportunities presented by technology-driven innovation compared to global peers, potentially impacting its overall attractiveness and performance in the post-Brexit landscape. This low exposure acts as a significant drag on its dynamism and competitive edge.
viewpoints.source_title: Brexit 10 years on: What it means for UK businesses today

demand_drivers.description: Changes to the Energy Profits Levy (EPL) and a renewed approach to licensing are needed to make projects investable in the UK Continental Shelf.
Maximising domestic production is a central objective of UK energy policy, driving investment in the UKCS to reduce reliance on imports.

demand_drivers.driver: Project delays and asset life extensions
demand_drivers.description: Resilience in current oil & gas production has been driven by these factors, suggesting a strong underlying need for new sanctioned investment.

new_opportunities.description: 111 additional projects identified in the UK Continental Shelf (UKCS) could extend infrastructure life and increase domestic energy supply, unlocking significant private capital.
Requires cost reductions in allocation rounds and targeted investment in domestic capability to strengthen the UK's position as a leader in offshore wind and attract capital.
Significant emerging investment opportunity over the coming decade (e.g., East Coast Cluster, HyNet), requiring a sustainable commercial environment to attract private capital at scale.

market_sizing.methodology: OEUK modelling based on data provided by operators, identifying 111 additional projects that could be unlocked with fiscal reform and a renewed licensing approach from 2027, attracting private capital investment in the UKCS.

pnl_drivers.description: Higher entry multiples (e.g., 11.8x EBITDA average in 2025, 18.1x for >$500mn deals) reduce the margin for error and make returns more dependent on operational improvements, especially with less leverage.
With reduced leverage and higher entry multiples, operating performance (e.g., EBITDA growth) must carry more of the load for value creation. Disciplined buyers achieve higher MOIC.
The post-2008 boom was 'powered by cheap financing and expanding deal multiples', indicating leverage historically boosted MOIC. Less leverage now means operating performance is more critical.

market_sizing.methodology: Globally, average buyout entry multiple (PPM of EBITDA). For larger transactions (>$500 million), multiples reached 18.1x EBITDA in 2025. Data covers 2010-2023 vintages for MOIC analysis and 2023-2025 for entry multiples.
market_sizing.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

demand_drivers.description: The need for AI infrastructure is rapidly accelerating, expanding the digital infrastructure category to include computing-power-intensive data halls, cooling systems, and AI-specific retrofits.
Abundant capital for scaled, well-understood assets, particularly core data centers and hyperscale-adjacent platforms, drives M&A activity.
Expansion of digital infrastructure beyond traditional communications assets to include chip producers, services, and software companies.

market_sizing.methodology: US data center transaction value, increased over threefold from $20 billion in 2024 to over $63 billion in 2025, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Global digital infrastructure M&A deals increased by more than 60% year-on-year in 2025.
market_sizing.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

demand_drivers.description: Record levels of order backlog and recovery in widebody aircraft demand drive production ramp-up, requiring significant investment.
Defence sector linkages provide robust order books and public spending support, benefiting the aerospace sector.
Investment in skills and technology is needed to win work on future platforms and secure the long-term health of the sector.

pnl_drivers.description: Elevated costs for energy, materials, and labour weigh on profitability and margins within the aerospace sector.
Limited access to affordable finance undermines growth and resilience, impacting industrialization and competitiveness for UK aerospace firms.

market_sizing.methodology: Private investment specifically in the UK Aerospace sector for 2024. Data estimates compiled by Oxford Economics in 2026, based on publications from MoD and ADS own sources.

demand_drivers.description: Over 80% of PE portfolio companies are undergoing transformations, with firms doubling operating groups since 2021 to drive value and requiring significant investment.
Building AI into portfolio-wide value creation engines, reducing re-underwriting time and improving cost/revenue performance, creates new demand for PE capital.
Periodic re-underwriting of investment thesis during hold periods is a mechanism for resetting ambition and identifying new opportunities, potentially leading to further capital deployment.

pnl_drivers.description: Valuation multiples at a record 11.8x EBITDA in 2025 mean operating performance must carry more of the load for value creation, shifting from reliance on leverage and multiple expansion.

Average hold periods now exceed 6.5 years, and only 19% of 2021 acquisitions sold by 2025, requiring sustained value creation efforts. Buyout distributions fell to 6% of AUM in 2025 from 16% in 2015-2019.
AI can reduce costs (e.g., content production by 40%, customer care by 15%) and enable new product launches, directly impacting P&L and improving portfolio company profitability.

market_sizing.methodology: Global private equity deal value, which rose 19% year-on-year to $2.6 trillion in 2025, making it the second-highest total on record. Global exit value climbed 41% to $1.3 trillion.
market_sizing.source_title: Unlocking full potential: Five practices reshaping PE value creation
